risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns: because the Company sources a large part of its range from international suppliers under the outsourced model, currency movement feeds straight into procurement cost and profitability, and the Threats section adds that dependence on imports exposes the Company to supply-chain disruptions.

MD&A Threats: intense competition from low-cost imports is compounded by zero customs duty on imports for OEMs, which raises competitive pressure on GPEL's own pricing directly with the customer segment it sells to.
risks.risk: Competition from low-cost imports, especially from China

risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns names both as significant risks; the Threats section reinforces the technology angle, with OEMs adopting new technologies and importing components in kit form, which can design GPEL's discrete components out of the bill of materials.

MD&A Risks & Concerns: fluctuations in commodity prices may impact input costs, delivery schedules and market demand. The Performance by Sector commentary shows this playing out - metal price and currency volatility made it 'challenging for the market to absorb price increases', hitting sales.
risks.risk: Commodity and metal price volatility, with limited ability to pass it through

risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns: maintaining adequate inventory levels across a wide product range is essential to meet customer requirements but increases working capital pressure - a structural cost of the distribution-led, many-SKU model.
risks.risk: Working-capital burden from carrying wide-range inventory

risks.note: Demand from Instrumentation & Industrial Electronics and EMS was weak in FY2025-26, with slower growth in electronic meters, adapters and EV chargers; separately, EMS players sourcing globally at highly competitive prices threaten to bypass GPEL's channel altogether.
risks.risk: Demand concentration in weak end-segments and channel disintermediation by EMS players

risks.note: Management states that geopolitical developments adversely affected market conditions during the second half of FY2025-26, on top of an already subdued market outside a relatively stronger first quarter.

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
